Subject: SIG follow-up: a few encryption clarifications and artifacts

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the quick SIG spreadsheet earlier. The review team picked a handful of follow-ups on encryption we want to close out before the next vendor meeting:

- In-transit: please confirm TLS versions you accept on hosted API endpoints and any allowed cipher suites (we need the minimum spec for our firewall rules).
- Private / Dedicated: do you support mTLS for customer-to-service connections and/or VPN only?
- At-rest: short description of envelope encryption (DEK/KEK separation), cipher/mode (we list AES-256-GCM) and whether authenticated encryption is used.
- KMS/HSM: which KMS provider do you use for CMKs (cloud provider KMS or self-hosted HSM)? Are CMKs HSM-backed?
- Rotation: your operational cadence for rotating CMKs (master KEK) and DEKs, and whether you provide logs we can ingest showing rotation events and key rewraps.
- Evidence: sample rotation log (CSV), HSM vendor attestation PDF, and a simple TLS cipher list file would be perfect.

Can you send these artifacts or tell me a target date? We need them for our SIG evidence packet by next Thursday (9/3).

Best,
Tim
Security Engineer
Acme Corporation

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, Tim Walton <tim.walton@acme-corp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: a few encryption clarifications and artifacts

Tim / Aisha — adding the technical answers below; attaching the cipher list and a short summary doc in the package.

1) In-transit (hosted API)
- Minimum accepted: TLS 1.2 with AEAD cipher suites, and TLS 1.3. We immediately disable known-weak ciphers (RC4, 3DES, AES-CBC w/o HMAC).
- Cipher list (attached tls_cipher_list.txt): we prefer TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (TLS1.3) and ECDHE-ECDSA/ RSA with AES_128_GCM / AES_256_GCM for TLS1.2.
- TLS termination: for hosted, TLS terminates at our edge (globally distributed load balancers) and we maintain TLS-internal connections to service clusters; mutual TLS is used for control-plane links only.

2) Dedicated/Private
- Dedicated instances can be configured for mTLS between customer VMs and our inference service. We also support customer-managed VPN and VPC peering. For BYOK/private deployments, TLS may terminate inside the customer's VPC depending on config.

3) At-rest encryption
- We use envelope encryption: each object/document encrypted with a Data Encryption Key (DEK) using AES-256-GCM. DEKs are themselves encrypted (wrapped) using a Key Encryption Key (KEK) (a CMK) stored in customer or Redwood KMS depending on deployment. Authenticated encryption is used to prevent tampering.

4) KMS / HSM
- Hosted default: we use vendor-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys (e.g., Cloud KMS with HSM protection). For enterprise BYOK we support customer-managed CMKs imported or created in a customer KMS/HSM (non-exportable).
- HSM attestation: we have vendor attestation outputs (FIPS/HSM vendor statement) — attached as hsm_attestation_acme_2026-07.pdf in the package.

5) Rotation cadence & logs
- DEK rotation: automated rewrapping of DEKs on a 30-day cadence by default (rolling), can be shorter per customer config.
- KEK/CMK rotation: typical operational rotation of CMKs is 12 months for master keys; customers can request more frequent rotation and we support automated rewraps.
- Rotation process: when a KEK rotation occurs we perform an automated rewrap of existing DEKs and emit a rotation event to audit logs. We retain rotation events for 1 year by default (longer retention available as an add-on).
- Evidence: we can export rotation events as a CSV showing timestamp, key_id, operation (rotate/rewrap), actor/service_account, and status. Sample: redwood_rotation_log_2026-08.csv (attached).

Operational notes:
- We never export plaintext CMKs. DEKs decrypted only inside memory of running inference process and are zeroized after use.
- For Dedicated/Private with BYOK, customers retain CMK control and we only receive wrapped keys as required.

If you want, Neha can provide a 2-minute sample of the rotation CSV schema so you can map fields to your ingestion pipeline.

— Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Tim — attaching a tiny sample CSV export and a short README explaining each column (rotation_log_sample.csv).

Notes: the CSV uses UTC timestamps (ISO 8601), key_id is the CMK/KEK identifier, op is one of {create, rotate, rewrap, retire}, actor is the principal that initiated the operation. Example row:
2026-07-14T02:17:45Z, projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/kr-01/cryptoKeys/cmkey-123, rewrap, serviceAccount:rotation-worker@redwood.iam

We redacted internal principals for the sample; full exports for attestation will include the service account names and trace ids.

Also small clarification: for hosted endpoints TLS termination at edge uses certs rotated on a 90-day cadence. We will include the cert rotation schedule in the ZIP.

Thanks — Neha
Security Operations Engineer
